joined_late.about: the captain joined the Hansa forty years after it was founded

Ancient Ruins Alpha.system: Tau Ceti, in the debris disk

Ancient Ruins Beta.system: Epsilon Indi, a moon of the cold giant Ab

Alien Signal Research Outpost Y.system: Sol, the outer system: a dish pointed at Lyra, past HD 178911

intro.from_cargo3.title: Seventy years early
text: The Gyrotron turned once under {origin.name}'s ship, and the dock clock says 2460. The Hansa is forty years old. You knew it at a hundred and ten.
You know how the Mandate ends. Said aloud, that gets you a cell, or a job with {serac}. You keep it to yourself, and you keep your old navigation computer.

intro.again.title: Again
text: {origin.name} has flown these years once already, as {origin.rank}, and walked away before the end.
The needle office has your face on file with another name under it. You let the clerk keep the mistake and buy a hauler with a loan, like the first time.

intro.colonel.title: Colonel, retired
text: {origin.name} took {serac}'s commission forty years ago and wore the Mandate's grey until the pension came. {serac} signed the pension himself. He has not aged a day.
The long sublight legs kept you younger than the calendar. The Mandate keeps your file open: a colonel with a hauler is either retired or working, and it has not decided which.

intro.veteran.title: The First Legion
text: The First Legion that {origin.name} helped make was folded into the Terran Mandate with all the others. Your medal is a Mandate medal now. Nobody asked you.
The Mandate has a file on you, and {serac} has read it. You buy a hauler without guns and book a place in a needle, like anybody.

intro.founder.title: Founder, on a pension
text: {origin.name} is one of the captains the Hansa was founded by, and the league pays a pension to prove it. Every year its accountants try to cut it.
Forty years on the calendar, fifteen on you: the long sublight legs saw to that. You want the needles more than the pension, so you buy a hauler and go to book a place.

intro.heading.title: The file
text: {origin.name} filed the course home from Scholz's Star forty years ago. The Institute stamped it received and put it on a shelf.
This month somebody took it off the shelf. The Concord's clerks will not say who. You buy a hauler with a loan and go to find out.

intro.tycoon.title: One more run
text: {origin.name} was the richest hauler of the decade, and then of the next. Retirement lasted until the money got boring.
You buy a ship far below your means and book the middle of a needle, where nobody will recognise you. Somebody always does.
{origin.name} paid for the portal at the Stellar Institute. Forty years later it is still the most expensive thing ever built that nobody can use.
You buy a ship far below your means and book the middle of a needle, where nobody will recognise you. Somebody always does.

intro.unfinished.title: Forty years on
text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, walked away from a career forty years ago, before it was finished. The long sublight legs kept you younger than the calendar.
The routes are forty years older than you remember. Ships cross between the stars in needles now, and the needle office wants a booking.

intro.fresh.title: A place near the tail
text: Every hauler starts the same way: a loan, a ship older than the loan officer, and a place booked in the next needle out of {place}.
The Hansa turned forty last month. Its founders' names are on the wall of the needle office. Yours is on a slot near the tail.

ch1.title: Forty Years On
text: Forty years after the Hansa was founded, the needles leave on schedule: a lead hauler pushing its asteroid, and a file of ships in its wake.

Between the stars you ride in a needle, booked at the Hansa's needle office when you travel. Inside a star system you fly on your own fuel. The Hansa, the Mandate and the Concord all watch who books where.

hansa.first_mark.title: The founders' wall
text: The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it, and the first Mark under glass: a pellet of metal with a registry number stamped into it.
Haulers touch the glass for luck on the way to their slots. You touch it too.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. Yours is the first, above the first Mark under glass.
The clerk looks from the wall to you and stands up. 'The league remembers who signed first,' she says.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. Yours is the eleventh, between two captains who died rich.
The clerk finds it after a while and puts a star on your booking.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. None of them is yours.
The clerk knows the story: the captain who stayed out. 'You can still join,' she says. 'It costs more now.'

choices.say: Take the founders' share (two Hansa bonds)
Leave the share in the league's chest
Touch the glass and go to your slot

hansa.targa.title: The master of the needle office
text: The master of the needle office is Grab {convoy_captain}, eighty-one and chewing liquorice root. She has run the convoys since before the needles had names.
'New captain,' she says, reading your slot. 'The middle is where you learn. The tail is where you learn faster.'
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. She sees your name on the list and crosses the floor herself, slower than she used to.
'I keep score,' she says. 'I still owe you a berth.'
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. 'Two barges, perishables, no tug,' she says before you open your mouth.
'I keep score.' She moves your next booking to the front without being asked.
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. She remembers the Cargolytes' raid, and who cut loose and ran.
She looks at your booking for a long time, then moves it to the tail.
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root.
'You left my barges at the dock,' she says, not looking up. 'Forty years ago. The perishables were melons.'

choices.say: Take the berth (ten jumps at the front for the middle's fare)
Tell her the score is even
Take the tail and say nothing

hansa.pell.title: {young_hauler.short} at fifty-nine
text: {young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. In the back room of the needle office he teaches new haulers how to book, where to sit, and what the Cargolytes take from the tail.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa, with a seat on the needle council and the same grin as at nineteen.
'You flew with me when I had nothing,' he says. 'Book us into the same needle and I'll take the place behind you.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. He pays back the ten thousand you lent him at nineteen, with forty years of interest at the Hansa's rate, worked out to the credit.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You took me back from the raiders,' he tells the young haulers around him. 'Nobody else would have. Remember that when somebody asks you.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. He remembers the captain who turned a nineteen-year-old away from the dock, and he is polite about it, which is worse.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa, with a scar along his jaw from a fight on a lane forty years ago.
'I was on the wrong side of it,' he says. 'So were you.' Then he buys you a drink.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You paid me to go away,' he says. 'I went. Then I came back with a ship.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You told me to keep my receipts and stay out of the tail,' he says. 'I still do. Mostly.'

choices.say: Tell him to stand the young haulers a round with it
Ask what the ship was called
You know how to sit in a needle

hansa.notebooks.title: {inspector.short}'s notebooks
text: {inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
The notebooks are a book now, sold at every needle office: The Manifests. The customs officer checking your hold quotes it at you, page and line.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor stops you at the gate with page nine: a 'processing fee', your name, the date, the amount. 'Bribery has no time limit,' he says. 'The fine has a size.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page nine, then page ten: fined in full, closed. 'Well,' he says. 'Off you go.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page sixty: the captain who opened her sealed case. She wrote that down too.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor has page seventy-two open: you told her about the Rootstock's big run. Customs records go public after thirty years, and the Rootstock read them.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor stops you at the gate with page forty-one. 'She wrote that your manifests were always right,' he says. 'She never wrote that about anybody else.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page sixty: you carried her case sealed and never opened it. The case put a quartermaster in prison.

choices.say: Pay the fine, with forty years of interest
Refuse: the inspector is retired, and so is the fee
Ask who else has read it
Ask for the page about salt

hansa.old_hand.title: An old hand
text: An old captain sits under the founders' wall, telling the young haulers how it was before the needles: {visitor.name}, {visitor.rank}, forty years retired.
'The middle of the file,' {visitor.name} tells you. 'Always the middle, until you can afford to be wrong.'

choices.say: Buy the old hand a drink
Listen, and go to your slot

rumour.gamma_coop.text: Gamma's underground farms feed three systems now. The miners' cooperative keeps an empty chair at its meetings for the captain who signed the farms over.

rumour.gamma_company.text: Gamma is a company town: the farms, the shafts and the canteen belong to one board. The miners call the farms 'the captain's gift', and they do not mean it kindly.

rumour.harp.text: The quantum harp has forty strings now. The Hansa's forecasts come from it, and the Mandate would very much like to know how.

rumour.insured.text: Every needle leaves insured. The underwriters have done well out of it for forty years, and they still tell the story of the flare lane.

rumour.bekkenheim.text: House Bekkenheim licenses the resonance every lead hauler jumps on. Fly past the Bekkenheim limit without a licence and you are a pirate, whatever you carry.

rumour.lighthouse.text: Every jump shows on the Mandate's gravity-wave observatories like a lighthouse. Smugglers fly decoys. The Mandate counts the decoys too.

rumour.tithe.text: The Cargolytes work the tail of every needle. Now and then they cut a container loose and call it the tithe. Some captains pay before they are asked.

rumour.santor.text: The drive in every lead hauler carries {santor}'s name. Ask at the needle office why, and the clerks change the subject.

rumour.jump_clocks.text: A jump takes minutes aboard and years outside. Haulers keep two clocks, and argue about which one the loan is on.

rumour.mandate.text: The Mandate's needles go first, and their decoys go first too. Civilian needles wait at the departure buoy while the grey ships form up.
